dossier.name: Bajaj Finance Limited

lines.text: Bajaj Finance reported a market capitalization of ₹6,67,889 Cr.
In FY26, net interest income reached ₹53,086 Cr while PAT stood at ₹19,332 Cr.
The company recorded an ROE of 18.0% and an ROA of 3.8% during FY26.

note.text: Between FY17 and FY26, total revenue expanded from ₹9,970 Cr to ₹81,985 Cr, while ROE moved from 22.0% to 18.0%.

citations.quote: In MSME, you've seen GNPA continue to deteriorate. What book is driving that? And also broadly, GNPA going up 10 basis points in the quarter, which areas you've talked about gold but any other areas that we should be thinking of in terms of where stress might be building?

citations.title: Q1 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: Do you see this kind of a structural improvement or this is again a cyclical kind of a mean reversion will happen? And if this is structural do you see that structurally the yields will see a compression because the credit cost is improving?

citations.title: Q4 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: Yes, so there, your number is gross loan provisions of INR 2,126 crores and then INR 260 crores of recovery. So the net loan provision is INR 1,866 crores. That INR 1,866 crores works out to 165 bps in 4Q. And against that, you're guiding for 145 to 160 bps next year, full year. Is that the right understanding?

claim.text: Asked in 8 of 8 calls. Latest: “What is the growth guidance and margin outlook given rate hike scenario and cost of funds?”

citations.title: Q2 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: So, what would be the growth guidance here onwards for near and medium term? So that's the first question? And second, in terms of the overall margins, cost of funds are down 9 basis points, but given that we are in the rate hike scenario, we had still seen some margin compression and NIMs on calculated basis appear to be down.

citations.title: Q1 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: So, the question is that fact that it was an excellent quarter, despite that, you've not seen any change in your assessment for FY'27.
